correctness.rationale: Vertex and dual-facet sign arrangements act on six and ten antipodal axes respectively. Section polygon vertices count primal edge sign cuts; shadow silhouette vertices count dual edge cuts. Inspected exact-Q(sqrt5) certificate constructs 20 facet normals, 30 primal/dual edges, 32 vertex-sign chambers and 92 facet-sign chambers, verifies no triple concurrence and the 20 T=12 triangle cone extreme rays all lie in S=6 shadow hexagon cones. Spherical excess and angles a=acos(1/3), b=acos(sqrt5/3), c=acos(1/sqrt5) yield four strictly positive cells summing to one. Fresh independent generic integer-grid normal scan corroborated four outcomes and T=12=>S=6, but only exact cone certificate supports ALL directions; nongeneric normals excluded.
residual_risks: Only regular icosahedron and same Haar normal; nongeneric great-circle boundaries have zero measure.
No claims for independently oriented planes, deformed polytopes or geometric areas.

originality.rationale: Existing separate icosahedron central-section Haar law and polar regular-dodecahedron shadow marginal do not determine their coupling. The surviving original contribution is exact cooriented cone containment yielding two impossible joint outcomes, conditional determinism and covariance; not individual marginal laws. No identified primary statement implies the containment; older stereology cone refinements remain a risk.
